title: Non-blocking follow-ups from frontend-fibonacci-auto-levels's PR #361 review
description: Tracked, non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #361 (frontend-fibonacci-auto-levels, the client-side Fibonacci retracement overlay on the Stock Detail price chart). See that PR's review comment and docs/tasks/frontend-fibonacci-auto-levels.json's review.comments for full context.

checklist.step: frontend/src/features/stocks/components/fibonacciLevels.ts's findFibonacciSwing keeps the FIRST bar it encounters at a tied extreme value (strict `>`/`<` comparisons in the scan loop), not the most recent one -- so when the visible range's highest high (or lowest low) recurs across more than one bar (e.g. a resistance level touched twice), the swing's recorded date for that extreme is the earliest occurrence, which can flip the computed `direction` (and therefore mirror-flip which actual price gets assigned to each ratio label) relative to what 'the more recent extreme gets 0%' is meant to produce. Example: bars day1 high=100/low=90, day2 high=95, day3 high=100 (ties day1), day4 low=80 -- the loop keeps day1 as highBar (day3's tying high never replaces it since the comparison is strict `>`), so direction is computed from day1 vs day4 instead of day3 vs day4. Decide and document the intended tie-break for this case explicitly (e.g. prefer the most recent bar on a tie, matching the spirit of the existing single-bar-tie rule already documented on `FibonacciSwing.direction`) and add a test case for it. Flagged by the code-review skill during PR #361's review; judged non-blocking there because it requires an exact price tie across distinct bars in the visible range (a narrow edge case for continuous real market data), affects only a purely cosmetic/non-signal overlay, and has no single documented canonical convention to violate.

frontend/src/features/stocks/components/metricHelpContent.ts's new `fibonacciHelp.interpretValue` has no direct unit test in metricHelpContent.test.ts, breaking this file's own established convention of a dedicated `describe('<name>Help.interpretValue', ...)` block per *Help object (every other Help export in this file has one). In particular its 'down' (downtrend swing) branch -- the `swing.direction === 'up' ? ... : ...` ternary's false arm -- is entirely untested by any spec in this PR (PriceChart.test.tsx's Fibonacci fixtures only ever produce an 'up' swing), which also left it as an actually-uncovered branch in metricHelpContent.ts's coverage report. A live browser walkthrough during PR #361's review manually confirmed the 'down' branch renders correct text (aggressively zooming the AAPL Stock Detail price chart produced a downtrend swing and the MetricHelp popover correctly read '...a downtrend swing (the high on ... came before the low on ...) -- levels above the low read as potential bounce/resistance levels'), so this is a test-coverage gap, not a known behavioral bug. Add a `fibonacciHelp.interpretValue` describe block to metricHelpContent.test.ts covering both the 'up' and 'down' branches and both degenerate-case strings (fewer than 2 bars, flat range).

frontend/src/features/stocks/components/fibonacciLevels.ts's `selectVisibleBars<T extends { date: string }>` re-implements the exact same `.filter((x) => x.date >= firstDate && x.date <= lastDate)` logic PriceChart.tsx's own private `selectVisibleIndicatorPoints` already has (just typed for `IndicatorHistoryPoint` instead of a generic `T`). Consider generalizing one into the other (e.g. making `selectVisibleIndicatorPoints` itself generic, or promoting a single shared helper) so the windowing semantics can't silently drift apart between the two call sites in future edits. Flagged by the code-review skill during PR #361's review as a minor reuse/simplification opportunity, not a bug.

decisions.decision: Fixed findFibonacciSwing's tie-break by changing the scan loop's strict `>`/`<` comparisons to `>=`/`<=`, so a later bar that ties the current extreme replaces it (keeping the most recent bar at a tied extreme, not the first). No change to the untied-case logic or to computeFibonacciLevels/FibonacciSwing.direction's own existing same-date tie-break (both left as-is). Added two new fibonacciLevels.test.ts cases (tied-high and tied-low) constructed so the tie-break actually flips the resulting `direction` relative to the old first-bar-wins behavior, not just the recorded date, to make the fix's effect unambiguous.
decisions.rationale: The `>=`/`<=` swap is the minimal, spec-consistent fix the checklist item itself proposed ('prefer the most recent bar on a tie, matching the spirit of the existing single-bar-tie rule already documented on FibonacciSwing.direction') -- iterating bars in their natural (chronological) order means a `>=`/`<=` comparison naturally keeps the last (most recent) bar seen at a given extreme value, with no extra bookkeeping needed. Rejected: tracking index/date explicitly and comparing dates on a tie (more code for the same result, since bars are already known to be chronologically ordered) and rejected: an explicit two-pass 'find max value, then find last bar with that value' approach (unnecessary extra pass over the same data).

decisions.decision: Added a fibonacciHelp.interpretValue describe block to metricHelpContent.test.ts (matching this file's per-Help-object convention) covering both degenerate null-swing cases (fewer than 2 bars, flat range) and both direction branches ('up' and 'down'), asserting on the swing-low/swing-high substrings, the direction-specific framing sentence, and a representative sample of the rendered per-ratio level list (0%/23.6%/100%) for each branch.
decisions.rationale: Matches the exact test shape every other *Help.interpretValue block in this file already uses (build a fixture value, assert `toContain` on the notable substrings of the rendered message) rather than a full exact-string `toBe` match, which would make the test brittle to any future non-semantic wording tweak to the surrounding sentence. Reused the exact swing fixtures and hand-computed level prices already verified in fibonacciLevels.test.ts's computeFibonacciLevels suite (120/90 range) instead of inventing new numbers, so there's one hand-verified source of truth for what those prices should be.

decisions.decision: Resolved the duplication by making PriceChart.tsx's private selectVisibleIndicatorPoints delegate to fibonacciLevels.ts's already-generic, already-exported selectVisibleBars (`return selectVisibleBars(points, firstDate, lastDate)`), rather than deleting selectVisibleIndicatorPoints and calling selectVisibleBars<IndicatorHistoryPoint> directly at its two call sites, and rather than moving the generic helper to a new shared utils module.
decisions.rationale: PriceChart.tsx already imports selectVisibleBars from fibonacciLevels.ts for the Fibonacci overlay itself, so the import-direction precedent (fibonacciLevels.ts as the generic windowing helper's home, PriceChart.tsx as a consumer) already exists in this codebase -- no new module or import cycle needed. Keeping selectVisibleIndicatorPoints's own name/signature/doc comment at both call sites (rather than inlining selectVisibleBars<IndicatorHistoryPoint> at each) preserves its own doc comment's context (the /indicators-vs-/history defensive-guard rationale, and being 'exported so two computations can't drift' -- referring to its own two internal call sites, not fibonacciLevels.ts) with the smallest possible diff, while still eliminating the actual duplicated filter logic the checklist item flagged. Rejected: promoting a brand-new shared module (e.g. a `visibleRange.ts` utils file) for a single one-line filter function -- more indirection than the size of the problem warrants, and CLAUDE.md/architecture docs express no existing convention calling for a shared-utils module at this granularity.
